# FAERS disproportionality as evidence (generated by experiments/fetch_faers_disproportionality.py — do not edit by hand)

Generated by `experiments/fetch_faers_disproportionality.py` on 2026-10-16 at commit 586828d from openFDA drug/event (data/raw/faers), data/processed/evidence_full_v4; do not edit by hand.

Source `FAERS-disproportionality`: 222 study drugs queried against 20,692,690 reports in the system; 2 drugs had no report naming them. **2,252 signals** (PRR >= 2, chi-square >= 4, at least 3 reports) and **117 absences** (ROR upper bound below 1 with at least 2,000 reports naming the drug) over 208 drugs; 811 reaction rows were set aside because the symptom is one the drug is indicated for, where disproportion measures the indication rather than the drug.

Spontaneous reports carry no exposure denominator, so a signal is disproportion against every other drug and an absence is under-reporting against background, not a rate; one report names several drugs, so counts are correlated across co-prescribed drugs. The rows join the assembled table through `--extra-reports` with the number of reports naming the drug in `rubric_log_sample_size`; the tier and the reliability fit decide their weight.
